**Pre-release for field testing.** macOS transparent mode (Beta) is now
available: after one install command, Safari, Chrome, Firefox, Discord
and every other app get the automatic DPI bypass with no proxy
settings and no DNS changes. Linux and Windows behavior is unchanged
from v1.1.0-rc1.

> **Validation status:** macOS transparent mode passes the full
> automated end-to-end test on real macOS machines (GitHub runners:
> macOS 14, 15 and 26 on Apple silicon, macOS 15 on Intel) with the
> real PF packet filter and launchd. It has **not yet been tested on a
> physical Mac, and not yet against real ISP DPI on macOS**. Please
> report how it works on your network.

## macOS (Beta)

Download `dpi-proxy-macos-arm64.zip` (Apple silicon) or
`dpi-proxy-macos-x86_64.zip` (Intel), double-click it, then in Terminal:

```sh
cd ~/Downloads/dpi-proxy-macos-arm64
sudo ./install.sh
dpi-proxy-ctl status
```

Then use Safari, Chrome, Firefox, Discord, … normally. If something
fails: `dpi-proxy-ctl diagnose discord.com` and `dpi-proxy-ctl logs`.
Uninstall: `sudo ./uninstall.sh` in the same folder. See
`MACOS-QUICKSTART.txt` in the ZIP.

The ZIP contains everything: `dpi-proxy` (OpenSSL linked in; needs
nothing but macOS 11 or newer), `dpi-proxy-ctl`, `install.sh`,
`uninstall.sh`, the launchd job, LICENSE and the quick start. No
Xcode, Homebrew, Git or Python.

How it works: dpi-proxy's own rules in the built-in macOS packet filter
(PF anchor `com.apple/dpi-proxy`; `/etc/pf.conf` and other rules are
never touched) route this Mac's HTTPS and DNS to the local service,
which applies the same DNS-over-HTTPS, TLS record fragmentation and
per-network learning as on Linux. A watchdog removes the rules the
moment the service stops or crashes (within 30 s if it hangs), so the
internet keeps working, just unbypassed. Details:
[docs/transparent-mode.md](https://github.com/kadireren7/dpi-for-everyone/blob/v1.2.0-rc1/docs/transparent-mode.md#macos).

### Validated (automated end-to-end test on real macOS machines — GitHub runners — with real PF and launchd)

- install from the extracted ZIP, launchd start, installer health check
- PF rules installed in dpi-proxy's anchor only; main ruleset and other
  anchors unchanged
- HTTPS interception; original destination recovery
- DNS for all apps answered via DNS-over-HTTPS; `localhost` and
  mDNS/Bonjour (`.local`) unaffected; local names go to the network's
  own resolver
- QUIC fallback (UDP/443 to known-blocked addresses refused)
- IPv6 interception (on the runners with IPv6)
- the bypass path (TLS record fragmentation)
- no redirect loops
- `dpi-proxy-ctl` status / diagnose / logs / strategy / start / stop /
  restart
- restart; stop → ordinary networking, PF exactly as before
- crash (SIGKILL) → fail-open at once, automatic restart by launchd
- hang (SIGSTOP) → rules removed by the watchdog, reinstalled on resume
- uninstall leaves no launchd job, files, settings, logs, processes, PF
  rules/tables or PF reference behind; clean reinstall

### Still pending

- a physical Mac (all tests ran on virtual machines on Apple hardware)
- real ISP DPI validation on macOS
- Wi-Fi changes, sleep/wake and captive portals on a real Mac (handled
  in code; not exercisable on CI machines)
- macOS 11–13 (built for them, not tested)

Known limitation: DNS servers with IPv6 link-local addresses
(`fe80::…`) are not intercepted. macOS keeps the (empty) PF anchor name
registered until the next restart after uninstalling; it contains no
rules.

## Linux, Windows

Unchanged. One internal change shared by all platforms: the platform
layer reports network-change events it can filter (no behavior change
on Linux/Windows). The full Linux and Windows end-to-end tests pass.

## Assets

- `dpi-proxy-macos-arm64.zip` — macOS transparent mode (Beta), Apple silicon
- `dpi-proxy-macos-x86_64.zip` — macOS transparent mode (Beta), Intel
- `dpi-proxy-windows-x86_64.zip` — Windows transparent mode (Beta) + SOCKS5
- `dpi-proxy-linux-x86_64` — Linux binary (install from source with `scripts/install.sh`)
- `SHA256SUMS`
